title: Bitcoin and ether edge higher, broader market slips, portfolio rises
paragraphs: Bitcoin edged up 0.4% over 24 hours to about $61,300, and ether gained 0.8% to $1,722. The broader market moved in the opposite direction: CoinGecko reported total crypto capitalization of $2.09 trillion, down 1.8%, with bitcoin representing 58.8% of the total. The modest gains in the two largest assets therefore sit alongside weakness across the aggregate market. They offer limited evidence of a broad recovery.

Visa Crypto Labs has released an experimental version of Visa CLI that lets eligible US cardholders verify AI agents and connect them to paid tasks. Agents can receive OUSD stablecoin rewards through Taskmarket when their work is accepted. Owners can set spending limits and pause agents. This gives stablecoin payments a concrete role in paying for software-assisted work, although access remains restricted and completing a task does not guarantee payment. Visa’s documentation also makes clear that card verification does not certify the quality of an agent’s work.

Fusionist’s ACE bridge suffered an exploit that spread into exchange trading. The Block’s on-chain analysis estimates that an attacker sold newly minted, unbacked tokens for about $2 million; subsequent traders drained roughly $3.7 million of backing tokens through the bridge. Gate confirmed the exploit and announced a rollback of affected ACE spot trades, alongside restrictions and planned delisting for its perpetual market. The consequences extend beyond the initial theft: holders face uncertainty about token validity, while exchange users face disrupted trading and settlement.

Stellar validators are scheduled to vote on the Bell upgrade next. The proposal would let smart contracts distinguish deposits for multiple customers, support verification of post-quantum signatures inside contracts, and introduce finer ledger timestamps. These changes could help custodians operate shared smart accounts and prepare infrastructure for later improvements. Approval is still pending. Bell would neither replace the network’s existing transaction signatures nor automatically make ledger production faster.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $54,300, comprising $8,840 in the active treasury and $45,454 in the Safe. Its marked value rose $461, or 0.9%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings are worth $37,668, around 69% of the total, and their unchanged balances account for $307 of that increase. The Safe also holds a $5,331 WETH/ARC pool, adding to ARC concentration. Beefy positions total $1,721 across several pools; ETH and wrapped ETH remain other significant exposures.

Aave holds about $5,892 of WETH collateral against $3,153 of USDC debt. Treasury and Safe health factors improved slightly to 1.79 and 1.43, from 1.78 and 1.42. Fluid remains the tightest lending position: about $155 net value, $1,067 of debt and an unchanged 1.03 health factor, leaving little room before liquidation risk becomes acute.
